QF.id: Evaluating Fund Performance and Fund Selection_11

question.text: Kavita invested Rs.10,000 and earned Rs.900 in one year. Deepak invested Rs.5,000 and earned Rs.500 in the same period. Who earned a higher percentage return?

answer.text: Kavita, because she earned more rupees
Deepak, because his percentage return is 10% versus Kavita's 9%
Both earned the same percentage return
Cannot be determined without knowing the fund NAV

explanation.text: The Logic: Percentage return = (Return on Investment / Original Investment) x 100. Kavita: (900 / 10,000) x 100 = 9%. Deepak: (500 / 5,000) x 100 = 10%. Deepak's percentage return is higher even though his absolute rupee gain is lower. The Trap: Option A confuses absolute rupee gain (Rs.900 > Rs.500) with percentage return. Option C is wrong because 9% and 10% are not equal. Option D is wrong because the investment amounts and rupee gains are given, so percentage return can be computed directly without NAV. Note: Distributor-style coaching wording removed; explanation rewritten in adviser-neutral terms using the Return on Investment / Original Investment x 100 formula.
